customer-ops: hey team — starting ~08:30 UTC our production integration (CUST-772) is seeing intermittent 524s on POST /v1/generate. ~1-3% of requests. Most calls return 200, a subset return 524 with no response body. SDK retries are firing and creating duplicate downstream events for customers. example rw request id: rw-req-20260312-4589. we've attached a minimal curl repro below. wondering if this is related to our token shape — we do a delegation wrapper that makes the Authorization header pretty long. removing the header in our test makes the failures go away. can we get help?

Maria G: thanks — escalating to SRE. can you confirm SDK version + whether you sit behind any proxy that might modify headers? also paste the raw -v curl output (response headers) for a failing request if you have it. i'll open a ticket with priority. :eyes:

customer-ops: sdk: node 2.1.3. we sit behind our API gateway which adds an X-Client-Trace header but shouldn't touch Authorization. reproduced locally with:

```
export LONG_TOKEN="<REDACTED_LONG_DELEGATION_TOKEN>"
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $LONG_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

most runs give 200, but occasionally we get:

```
* Connected to api.redwood.com (34.12.45.67) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> Authorization: Bearer <LONG_TOKEN>
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 16
> 
< HTTP/1.1 524 Origin Time-out
< Server: redwood-edge
< Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2026 08:46:27 GMT
< x-rw-request-id: rw-req-20260312-4589
< 
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.com left intact
```

removing Authorization header (or swapping to a short-lived ephemeral token) returns 200 consistently.

Alex SRE: thanks — that's helpful. 524 means the edge timed out waiting for the origin. there are two likely hypotheses: (1) our upstream service does hit a slow path for certain token shapes (parsing cost), (2) our edge/proxy is mishandling very large Authorization header values and that triggers a connection/timeout race. can you run tcpdump or provide the full open/close sequence (we need the timing)? also paste any x-rw-trace or span ids if available. i'll pull edge logs for the x-rw-request-id.

customer-ops: attaching -v timestamps and the raw tcpdump snippet. we can reproduce 524 by running the curl loop below (run ~100 times).

```
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LONG_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"input":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate || echo "err"
  sleep 0.2
done
```

we see ~2-4 failures per 100.

Priya (infra): i've seen similar where envoy/nginx header buffer config caused the proxy to pause or reset while the backend waited, which can surface as 524s from our edge. also possible that our token parser in the auth service goes into a slow codepath for extremely long delegation chains. agree with Alex — we need edge logs for rw-req-20260312-4589 and a couple more failing ids. can you share 2-3 more failing request ids?

customer-ops: more ids: rw-req-20260312-4620, rw-req-20260312-4681. attaching raw headers from a failing and a succeeding request — the only notable difference is Authorization length.

Maria G: workaround options while we investigate: (a) rotate to a shorter token via token-exchange (we can assist) (b) temporarily suspend SDK automatic retries for that integration to avoid duplicate downstream events (c) route you to a dedicated host with relaxed header buffers (ops can do this short-term). which would you prefer? :slightly_smiling_face:

customer-ops: for now please: 1) suspend automatic retries for the customer id to avoid duplicate billing/events, 2) help with a token-exchange flow we can implement quickly. we'll run the curl loop again after you suspend retries.

Alex SRE: opening a P1 incident and pulling logs for the three request ids. i'm also starting an urgent config change to increase envoy header_buffer_size and client_header_buffer_size on the edge to see if that reduces the failure rate. ETA ~45m for config rollout. i'll post progress here and include traces.

deploy-bot: started rollout: envoy/increase-header-buffers -> rollout_id: rb-20260312-17
deploy-bot: rollout complete: rb-20260312-17 (applied to edge pool region-us-west)

Alex SRE: patch applied to us-west edge. i've pulled logs for rw-req-20260312-4589 and the pattern shows the connection established -> backend parse stall -> connection timed out. with the header buffers increased we should avoid the proxy-level stalls. i'll keep monitoring.

Maria G: i've disabled SDK retries for CUST-772 in the tenant config and created a support ticket for billing/duplicate requests — please send a list of any request ids you consider duplicated and we'll credit them.

Josh L: following up for process — add an alert rule for customer 5xx rate >0.5% over 15m and add a dashboard metric for Authorization header length distribution at the edge. this should help catch regressions.

customer-ops: after the change we reran the 100-loop and failures dropped to 0-1 per 100 (was 2-4). massively improved. we'll keep monitoring for 24h and confirm. thanks @Maria G @Alex SRE @Priya (infra) — leaving thread open until tomorrow.

support_lead: noted — we'll file the post-incident actions: (1) add header-length metric, (2) add retry-safety guidance in SDK README, (3) follow up with infra to harden auth parser. closing the P1 when customer confirms 24h stable.

customer-ops: thanks all, will report back tomorrow. :raised_hands:
